Summary (auto):
- Borealis is evaluating exit/port from OpenAI/Anthropic for customer support and fraud detection features. Primary concerns: data residency, KMS integration, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and predictable latency for customer chat.
- They run 250k token-equivalent requests/day with 95th p99 latency target of 300ms for short-turn chat (prompt+response). Currently using OpenAI + a vLLM cache layer for internal tooling.
- Redwood options discussed: Hosted API for initial pilot, Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and SLA, Private (VPC/on-prem) for high-regulated flows.
- Agreed next steps: micro-benchmark, security docs, pricing spreadsheet, follow-up on private deployment feasibility.

Topics: governance, KMS/HSM, escape hatch/private deploy, vLLM/TGI compatibility, benchmark plan, timeline (POC in Oct/Nov)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Samira, i'm the AE on the account from Redwood Inference. we've got Jae and Marco here from our engineering team. how's everyone?
[00:16] Ryan: hi, thanks. i'm Ryan, head of ML at Borealis. quick intros on our side: Amira runs platform, Derek infra, Priya is our privacy lead, tommy on sre.
[00:27] Samira: awesome. want to do a quick agenda? i'll cover product options and pricing outlines, Jae will do a short compatibility/latency Q, then we can dig into compliance.
[00:37] Amira: yep sounds good.
[00:41] Jae: cool, i'll start with what we typically see in these port-outs — okay so the usual mix is OpenAI on customer chat, anthropic for safety functions, and then sometimes folks run vLLM or TGI locally to get lower latency for internal tools. is that similar to you?
[00:56] Ryan: yep that's basically us. we also have a vLLM caching tier in front of OpenAI for frequently asked questions — it's reduced cost but we've been hitting memory pressure and ops churn.
[01:11] Jae: makes sense. two big things to check: model compatibility (do your prompts and evals run with Redwood-hosted models) and runtime escape-hatch — i.e., if you need to move to private or dedicated with same API and rollbacks.
[01:26] Derek: important for us: we can't send PII outside certain regions. we need to evaluate a private deployment or dedicated pools in region, and key management has to be customer-controlled for some workloads.
[01:39] Samira: absolutely. Redwood Private supports a VPC control plane and on-prem options, and we integrate with KMS — we have customers using customer-managed KMS/HSM. we'll share the KMS integration guide after the call.
[01:52] Priya: can you confirm retention for prompts and logs in hosted mode? our compliance team wants explicit TTLs and audit logs, plus SOC2 artifacts.
[02:03] Marco: yes, hosted has configurable retention and we emit audit logs per request. for high-security flows you'd typically go to Dedicated or Private where logs can be routed to your syslog or cloud storage under your control.
[02:17] Ryan: short question on eval parity — we run a taxonomy of prompts (about 1200 evals) and need to make sure output quality matches baseline from OpenAI and Anthropic. how disruptive are model diffs?
[02:30] Jae: good one. we usually do side-by-side evals with the customer's prompt set. sometimes there are style differences, but we support model-weight pinning and can route to fallback variants to maintain parity. the plan would be: run micro-benchmark with your eval set and report regressions.
[02:48] Amira: and how fast can that happen? we want results before the procurement window in early Oct.
[02:55] Samira: we can run a first pass in 72 hours if you provide the prompt pack and a small sample workload. Jae — is that right?
[03:03] Jae: yeah 48–72 hours for the initial run, then another week for deeper analysis if we find diffs. we'll provide a spreadsheet with token costs, latencies, and a regression summary.
[03:16] Tommy: latency — you mentioned p99 latency targets, what's realistic on Hosted vs Dedicated? our customer-facing chat needs p99 < 300ms for short responses.
[03:28] Marco: okay so there's two parts: model inference latency and network overhead. for short-turn chat (< 256 tokens) Hosted in region typically yields 150–300ms p99 for optimized models; Dedicated can get you lower variance and SLA-backed numbers because of reserved GPU pools; Private (on-prem) is best for sub-100ms if you colocate near your frontends and run a reduced model.
[03:50] Derek: are you supporting vLLM or TGI-based runtimes for private deploy? we currently use vLLM with some custom kernels.
[03:58] Jae: we support compatibility with vLLM/TGI artifacts — model formats and kv cache patterns — but there are nuances in kernel selection and quantization. we can ingest your checkpoint and run a compatibility test. sometimes we find differences in past-key-values handling that affect long-context tasks.
[04:18] Ryan: ok noted. what about fallback routing — like if hosted capacity is saturated, can requests failover to a cheaper model or different region without user-visible regressions?
[04:31] Marco: yes, smart routing is a Redwood feature — routing by policy (latency, cost, region). we can configure automated fallback to compatible model variants. there will always be some output variance, so we recommend canary and A/B rollouts tied to your eval checks.
[04:46] Priya: on the security side, do you have SOC2 and ISO artifacts we can review? plus encryption at rest and in transit?
[04:55] Samira: yes, SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 cert, and we encrypt data in transit with TLS and at rest with customer keys where needed. we'll attach the compliance pack.
[05:07] Amira: for the pilot, what's the recommended start: Hosted or Dedicated? we want a quick POC but also to limit data leaving our control.
[05:16] Jae: suggested path: start with Hosted for speed-of-onboarding for lower-risk prompts (non-PII). run eval parity and micro-benchmarks. for regulated flows, spin up Dedicated capacity in your region and then move to Private for the highest assurance.
[05:30] Ryan: what about cost modeling — how do we evaluate token cost vs dedicated monthly commit?
[05:36] Samira: we'll send a pricing spreadsheet showing per-token hosted costs, and example reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated with commit tiers; that will include burst and autoscale policy cost examples.
[05:48] Tommy: one operational question — do you provide per-token tracing or trace id so we can correlate SRE traces with downstream logs?
[05:56] Marco: yes, we include request-level tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdowns in the Console. you can export traces to your tracing system.
[06:06] Derek: for Private, how invasive is the control plane? we have air-gapped lanes for payments processing, prefer minimal footprint.
[06:14] Jae: we have two private models: VPC-hosted control plane where control plane talks over secure peering and you host inference nodes, and a fully on-prem package. the on-prem is heavier but supports air-gapped installs; the VPC option is often a good compromise.
[06:29] Priya: regarding KMS/HSM — can we bring our HSM for key wrapping?
[06:34] Marco: yes, customers have used BYOK via cloud KMS plus HSM integration. we'll include the KMS/HSM integration doc.
[06:41] Ryan: procurement will want an escape-hatch clause — if Redwood hosted changes TOS or model behavior we need a plan to pivot to private within X weeks. is there a standard playbook?
[06:52] Samira: we maintain an escape hatch playbook for enterprise — includes model export guidance, sample infra provisioning scripts, and recommended rollback timelines. we'll share a redacted playbook. timeline for full pivot depends on model sizes and infra readiness but we aim for a staged porting plan of 4–8 weeks for most customers.
[07:10] Amira: 4–8 weeks — that aligns with our risk tolerance. for the POC we'd want a pilot with scoped traffic and an SLA.
[07:18] Samira: yes, we can do a timeboxed POC with a dedicated pool and success criteria around latency, cost, and eval parity.
[07:25] Ryan: speaking of parity, are there guardrails or eval alerts if model quality regresses after a rollout?
[07:32] Jae: Redwood Optimize ties model metrics to your eval sets and raises regression alerts. you can auto-fallback to the previous model or route to a fallback family.
[07:44] Priya: quick question — data residency — if we choose Hosted, can you guarantee EU-only residency for certain requests?
[07:52] Marco: yes, region routing policies exist. you can pin requests by region or tenant to EU-only infrastructure. for stricter needs, Dedicated in-region or Private is preferred.
[08:02] Derek: jotted notes — we have to provide sample traffic (30k req/day) and top 50 prompts, plus our compliance Q list. we'll put that into a Google Drive.
[08:12] Samira: perfect, send that over and we'll get started.
[08:16] Jae: one more nuance — if you're using vLLM locally, the KV cache semantics can differ on offload. if you rely heavily on prefix caching, we should benchmark that path specifically.
[08:27] Ryan: noted. we'll include the vLLM configs.
[08:31] Amira: timeline question — procurement window is mid-october; we'd like a recommendation by Oct 6.
[08:38] Samira: we'll target sharing the initial benchmark and docs by Sept 29, and then a recommendation package by Oct 6.
[08:44] Tommy: any blockers on our side? none beyond providing artifacts.
[08:48] Priya: would like to review the SOC2 and the escape-hatch playbook before any PII is sent.
[08:55] Samira: understood, we'll gate PII until the legal/compliance review.
[09:00] Ryan: ok sounds good. last thing — do you have any customers in financial services who have done a similar migration? references?
[09:08] Samira: yes, we have a regulated fintech that did staged migration last quarter; i'll provide a redacted case study and a reference contact with permission.
[09:16] Amira: great.
[09:18] Samira: recap of next steps: I'll share pricing and compliance pack, Jae will run micro-benchmarks with your eval set, Marco will attach KMS and private deploy docs, and we'll reconvene week of Oct 5 to discuss pilot constructs. any other items?
[09:33] Derek: no. thanks.
[09:35] Ryan: thanks everyone.
[09:38] Samira: thanks all — we'll follow up via email with artifacts.
